lens: STORY & CURIOSITY (promo): hook in the first seconds, rhythm over ~90 s, one idea per beat, payoff, a clear end card and call to action; would a buyer want to try it?
ledgerCheck: Round 1: film.json stages.fixes is empty and qa/reviews/ had no earlier rounds, so there are no fixed / partial / skipped ids to verify.
summary: The arc works for a promo. It opens on a promise, introduces the product, builds a fast triplet of always-on features, turns into the dark 'some bugs only exist in time' register at 35.8 s, gives two real bugs with exact numbers, has a quiet agent beat, then a triad payoff and an end card. The turn (ch05-s01) and the counter that stops dead on 258 are the film's best minutes. Five things hold it back. (1) Two always-on proof shots use the wrong crops: ch04-s01 shows a clipped 'Test Runs / Playwright' tab sliver where the schedule chip should be, and ch04-s02 shows the owner-named Production URL and 'Delete environment' under the word 'staging'. (2) The USP sentence, 'A time-travel recording can', has no picture of what the time-travel recording sees. (3) The 'kept starting over' payoff of the 258 bug does not read in the frames. (4) The unnarrated agent beat is too small to read. (5) The end card shows the URL but no action, and never shows the spoken promise. The hook is clean but sells only convenience: the differentiator arrives at 43 % of the runtime.

issues.problem: Wrong crop. Instead of the spec's 'Add environment' label and its grey line, the floating strip shows the Production environment card: the owner-named URL 'collaborative-ai-editor.brett-lamy.workers.dev', a clipped 'Production' badge and a 'Delete environment' button, all on screen for the whole 3.1 s. The spec says nothing above recording y 250 may appear and the owner URL must stay out. Three pink rectangles also stay stuck on the URL line from +0.08 s to the end; they look like the pills' ghost origins. A buyer hears 'against staging' while reading 'Production'.
issues.fix: Re-crop to take schedule tape 11000 → 11458, crop {x:300, y:266, w:420, h:54} (the 'Add environment' label and the 'Add production, staging, development, preview, or local co…' line). Verify on the sheet at +0.1 s, +0.7 s and +2.3 s that no URL, badge or button is visible. Lift the three pills from the words 'staging', 'preview' and 'local' in that grey line, and delete the stuck pink placeholder rectangles.

issues.problem: The name tag under the big '3:00 AM' is a clipped tab strip ('est Runs … Playwri', letters cut by the crop edges), not the real 'Tue at 3:00 AM · America/New_York' schedule chip. The red-pink underline at b-schedule (+2.70 s) runs under 'Test Runs'. The only product proof of scheduling never appears, and the sliver reads as a rendering glitch.
issues.fix: Measure the chip box again on the rr-sheet frame at tape 11458 (the crop at {1050,166,245,32} is landing on the tab bar, so the frozen frame's layout or scale is off). Show the whole chip at about 735 stage px wide with no cursor, and run the underline under 'Tue at 3:00 AM'. Check +0.79 s, +2.70 s and +4.00 s on the sheet.

issues.problem: The film's core USP, 'A screen recording can't see that. A time-travel recording can.', is only half illustrated. 'screen' gets the video-frame outline that keeps 2 squares. 'A time-travel recording can' cuts straight to the root-cause crop, so the viewer never sees what the time-travel recording sees (all 27 renders, including the 25 that changed nothing). The payoff of the differentiator is told but not shown.
issues.fix: On 'time-travel' (about +5.5 s), fade the video-frame outline and sweep the kit rewind playhead across the grid so all 27 squares re-light: the 25 hollow ones fill white and the 2 red ones stay red. Add a small label of ours, 'all 27 renders'. Then match cut to the ROOT CAUSE crop on 'can', and raise holdAfter 0.5 → 1.0 s so '{ root cause }' still reads for at least 1.5 s (runtime has 6 s of headroom under the 90 s target).

issues.problem: The explanatory half of the 258 bug does not read. Under L0508 ('It never saved its place, so it kept starting over.'), the frames at +5.04, +5.67, +6.12, +7.21 and +7.87 s are nearly identical. The bookmark flag's three snap-backs on 'never', the underline on 'place' and the 258-bar flash-back on 'starting' are too small or too brief to register, so about 3 s sits static on the counter.
issues.fix: Make the bookmark flag at least 28 px and give each try at least 80 px of forward travel before it snaps back to −1, spaced across 'never … place' (about +5.1, +5.4, +5.7 s). On 'starting', snap the counter 258 → 0 and let it race back up in about 0.5 s while the bars re-draw from the left, so 'starting over' is literal. Verify on the sheet at +5.2, +5.6, +7.3 and +7.6 s.

issues.problem: The unnarrated developer/critic beat is too small to carry its meaning. At scale 0.6, the card names, the '▶ replay recording' chip (about 10 px text at 1080p; at +0.79 s it overlaps the developer card's edge) and the 'not yet' / 'good' pills fall under the 22 px floor. With no narration, the chip label is the only thing that says the critic is judging a Replay recording, which is the whole point of the brief's beat.
issues.fix: Keep the corner placement and the subtlety, but scale agentPair to about 0.8. Set chip and verdict text to at least 22 px, and have the chip travel along the rail clear of both cards (it should never overlap a card edge). Hold each verdict at least 1.0 s. Verify on the sheet at +0.8, +1.5, +3.0 and +3.8 s.

issues.problem: The end card's call to action is soft. 'qa.replay.io' types in under the lock-up, but there is no verb or next step, and the spoken promise 'Catch bugs that only exist in time' (the film's hook) never appears on screen. The '▶ recording' chip glued beside the logo reads as a stray UI badge. A buyer sees a brand and a URL, not an invitation.
issues.fix: Close the loop with ch02-s01. On 'Catch', type 'qa.replay.io' into the same typed-prompt field, with the caret, that opened 'Point it at your app', and add a small eyebrow above it: 'Point it at your app'. Optionally let 'only exist { in time }' echo in small type under the tagline as the pad rings out. Either retire the '▶ recording' chip once it lands, or let it dock into the prompt field.

issues.problem: The hook sells convenience only. 'Imagine end-to-end tests you never write. Or remember to run.' is clean, but the film's distinctive hook (the brief's 'some bugs only exist in time') isn't planted until 35.8 s, 43 % in. Nothing in the first 7.5 s hints that this product sees something other test tools can't, so a skimming buyer has no reason to stay through the feature run.
issues.fix: Plant the turn early without new narration. In ch01-s01, make one of the drifting hairlines a faint frame ribbon with the red-pink rewind playhead running backwards across it for about 0.6 s in the hold after 'run.' (the same object ch05-s01 pays off). In ch01-s03, make the third stamp the 67 ms bug's red 'Open' chip, which it already is, and hold it a beat longer. If a line change is allowed, L0101 → 'Imagine end-to-end tests you never write. Or remember to run. That catch what a screenshot can't.' (adds about 1.8 s; runtime stays under 90 s).

issues.problem: 11.3 s on one bug page, the longest shot in an 84 s promo. From +4.3 s to +8.7 s the frame barely changes. The Replay player plate is a large black void, the 67 ms bar and frame strip occupy a thin band in its middle, and the dense jargon title ('RTK-Query … memo-less react-router Link components') dominates the top third.
issues.fix: On 'Sixty-seven' (b-ms67, +3.57 s), zoom 1.0 → 1.5 onto the player plate so the frame strip and the '67 ms' bar fill most of the frame. Light each dropped frame as 'Four dropped frames' is spoken; the music hole at 44.5 s already marks the moment. Ease back to 1.0 on 'No click' so the struck-through cursor has room. Keep the title's '67ms' underline visible at the top edge during the zoom.

issues.problem: The strongest proof of 'fully managed' in the footage, 'Insights: 89 explorations · 1151 journeys', is a faint grey footnote at the bottom of the step list (about 12 px). It is never pulled out, even though L0302 says 'user journeys'.
issues.fix: On 'journeys' (L0302), lift '1,151 journeys' off the Insights line as a kit pill, in the same style as 'hosted by Replay' in ch04-s01, and settle it to the right of the list. Keep the number exact and the source line visible.

issues.problem: At b-pill (+1.37 s), the zoom's red-pink underline runs through the 'Environment' column header like a strikethrough, and the braces sit over the header instead of the PR #3 badges. All eight rows read 'PR #3: PR #3', so 'every pull request' is shown as one PR repeated.
issues.fix: Anchor the braces and underline under the purple 'PR #3' badge column (row 1), not the header. If any run in the account's data belongs to a different PR, prefer a crop that shows two PR numbers; otherwise leave the rows and keep the pill wording as it is.

issues.problem: The typed URL grows leftward from the right frame edge. At +0.71 s 'https://|' sits about 1.5 % from the right edge, with a blurred ghost line to its left, and only reaches a near-centred position when typing ends. The prompt reads as off-balance in the film's first product beat.
issues.fix: Anchor the typed text at its final left x (centred for the full 'https://staging.your-app.dev') so it types left-to-right, and remove or sharpen the blurred ghost text to its left.

issues.problem: The root-cause clause crop shows the product's literal Markdown backticks ('`SidebarProjectList` trees'). It is real product text, but a buyer reads it as a glitch in the film's resolution card.
issues.fix: Crop the clause from 'trees are not memoized' only, keeping the braces around 'are not memoized', and name 'SidebarProjectList' in our kinetic label above it ('{ root cause }' → 'root cause · SidebarProjectList'). The product text is not edited.

issues.problem: Rhythm in 13.9–35.8 s is very dense: about 11 capabilities in 22 s, 7 lines flagged fast (190–199 wpm), and L0401 and L0404 each carry two to three ideas. Promo energy is right, but 'reviewed … what's slow', the line that sets up ch05, gets no air before the tape-stop.
issues.fix: Spend the 6 s of runtime headroom: holdAfter +0.3 s on ch03-s01 and ch04-s02, and +0.4 s on ch04-s03 before the tape-stop, so 'and what's slow' lands with a beat of room. Music re-fits to the new clock.

issues.problem: The lift at about 70–73 s is the loudest music in the film (-15.4 LUFS momentary at 70.3 s), and the mix QA shows L0601 at only 8 dB over the music (lineMasking warn), with L0602 at 9.8. The payoff and tagline lines are the ones the buyer most needs to hear.
issues.fix: Hold the 16th-pluck arpeggio and the open hats back about 2 dB under L0601 and L0602, and let the lift bloom in the gaps (72.8–73.1 s and after 'managed'). Target at least 10 dB of line-over-music on both.

best_moments: ch05-s01 (35.8–38.6 s): the tape-stop into plum, the frame ribbon with a playhead running backwards, and '{ in time }' landing exactly as the playhead stops. A real turn that changes the film's register.
The four-beat hole in the score (44.5–46.5 s) on 'Four dropped frames': the music itself drops frames. A smart sound-story idea.
ch05-s04: the request counter racing to 258 over 16th hats and stopping dead on 'fifty-eight', under the real bug title. The most memorable number in the film.
ch05-s03: the 67 ms bar shattering into a 9 × 3 grid, 25 hollow and 2 red, with '25 of 27 renders changed nothing'. A clean, honest picture of an invisible bug.
ch06-s01: 'every run / a recording · every bug / a root cause · every fix / rerun to confirm' woven over the collage. A tidy triad payoff that rhymes with the agent beat before it.
ch01-s03: '{ intro▢▢▢ducing }' flickering real product stamps in its gap before closing into the Replay QA mark. Faithful to the reference promo and on brand.
